decisions.statement: A page of the renamed type takes the new slug where the old slug named its type.
A page type's own file takes the new slug where the old slug opened its name.
Every file a page claims is carried with that page.
A file naming the old slug nowhere is refused rather than left behind.
A file landing where a body already sits is refused.
The pages are read from the index once rather than once for each page.
The key a page states its type under is restated as text rather than through a parse.
A slug is written into that key as the source spells a string rather than bare.
A page stating its type under both keys has both keys restated.
Nothing here says what follows a file to where that file landed.

definition: where every file a page type and its pages hold lands once that page type is renamed
